newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs rangebound, shorter maturities sold.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs rangebound, shorter maturities sold.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds languished in quiet trading on Monday afternoon, with no fresh news to stir the market into action and both the U.S. bond market and German Bunds failing to provide much of a lead.
By 1515 GMT the 10-year OLO was yielding 5.74 percent compared to 5.75 late Friday and unchanged from Monday morning. Its premium over Bunds edged out one basis point to seven bp.

Dealers said the only area to see much activity had been the short end of the yield curve. "We've seen some good selling in the three to five year maturities, but the others have been quiet," one said.
He pointed to the background of a weaker franc and higher short term money rates as a reason for this flattening of the OLO yield curve.

The Treasury's OLO exchange auction will provide the market with a focus on Tuesday, though some dealers expected only a small amount of interest to be shown after the Treasury netted a relatively large 61 billion francs at the previous excahnge auction in February.
The Treasury will offer OLOs maturing in April 1999, March 2001, March 2005 and March 2007 - the 10-year benchmark, in exchange for May 1997 and August 1997 maturities.
